header_summary:
Three critical security vulnerabilities have been identified and patched in recent Bitcoin Core releases, including a mempool inconsistency (CVE-2025-62861), Tor whitelist misapplication (CVE-2025-62860), and a witness malleation issue (CVE-2025-62859). Users are strongly advised to upgrade to the latest versions to maintain network integrity, with further details provided on the [official disclosure pages](https://bitcoincore.org/en/security-advisories/).

Testnet 5 genesis block mining is scheduled alongside the mainnet retarget event, introducing structural changes to simplify pooled mining and align block format with previous genesis blocks. Documentation and access details are available for participants interested in contributing hashrate, as outlined in the [official guide](https://gist.github.com/ajtowns/ebb148819c6028387271e6f0dce5e1da) and relevant [pull requests](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pull/2347).

A comprehensive framework for upgrading Bitcoin Script is proposed, centered on Tapleaf 0xc2 and five foundational BIPs—including general covenants, transaction introspection, and reusable macros—enabling advanced scripting features while preserving backward compatibility and static analysis guarantees ([BIP 440](https://github.com/jmoik/bips/blob/gsr-full/bip-0440.mediawiki), [reference implementation](https://github.com/bitcoin-gsr/bitcoin/tree/gsr)). The proposals are designed as a single soft fork, and open questions remain regarding potential impacts on network fairness and security.

Decentralized mining pool protocols and coinbase payout mechanisms are advancing, with new schemes such as payment hubs, Rolling Coinbase Aggregation, and sharechain UTXO trading—each addressing scalability, fairness, and attack resilience in unique ways ([Open Mining Stack](https://www.256foundation.org/), [Braidpool](https://github.com/braidpool/braidpool/blob/8d3c5198593d691f50ae5238cdaee215f4213cda/docs/braidpool_spec.mdpayout-update)). However, technical and economic challenges persist, especially under identity splitting and Miner Extractable Value risks.

Standardization efforts for co-signer spending policies aim to improve auditability and portability in Bitcoin custody by introducing a common, vendor-agnostic policy framework. This approach leverages existing protocol features and always includes a timelocked fallback, with real-world interoperability tests required before adoption as a practical standard ([discussion](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/bip-draft-co-signer-spending-policies/2955/12)). Additionally, new educational resources and guides clarify address compatibility and Taproot implications for users ([Gem Wallet documentation](https://docs.gemwallet.com/blockchains/bitcoin/bitcoin-address-types-bc1q-and-bc1p)).

recent_posts.title: Three Bitcoin Core security advisories
recent_posts.summary: - Three Bitcoin Core vulnerabilities have been fixed in version 29.2 and later releases.  - These flaws include risks related to mempool inconsistency, Tor connection whitelisting, and witness checks.  - Users and node operators should promptly upgrade to supported releases containing the necessary security patches.

recent_posts.title: Testnet 5 launch
recent_posts.summary: - The testnet5 genesis block will be mined at week’s end alongside the mainnet retarget event.  - Genesis block structure changes enable easier pooled mining and restore prior block format conventions.  - Block height encoding inconsistencies between implementations may cause chain initialization issues at low heights.

recent_posts.title: [Proposal] Tapleaf 0xc2: An overview of the Great Script Restoration (GSR)
recent_posts.summary: - Five interrelated proposals define Tapleaf 0xc2, restoring and expanding Bitcoin Script functionalities.  - The framework introduces transaction introspection, advanced script primitives, and computational budgets, ensuring backward compatibility.  - Static analysis guarantees, fixed costs, and extensive resources support a coordinated soft fork upgrade and ongoing discussions.

recent_posts.title: Should wallets default to Taproot or SegWit receive addresses while some services still reject bc1p?
recent_posts.summary: - A new section explains bc1q and bc1p addresses, highlighting compatibility and transaction flexibility.  - A concise troubleshooting guide now assists users resolving “invalid address” issues with bc1p addresses.  - Linked resources provide detailed insights into Taproot and advantages of various Bitcoin address formats.

recent_posts.title: Decentralized Coinbase Payout Protocols (DCPP): A Framework for Discussion
recent_posts.summary: - Decentralized mining protocols must address scaling, attack surface, and payout logic limitations for effective operation.  - Direct coinbase payouts face both technical constraints and fairness challenges like the Rich List Attack.  - Proposed solutions shift, rather than eliminate vulnerabilities, demanding careful design for security and fairness.

recent_posts.title: [BIP Draft] Co-signer Spending Policies
recent_posts.summary: - Bitcoin co-signing solutions lack standardization, causing vendor lock-in and poor auditability for users.  - An open, portable policy format is proposed, enabling standardized, auditable co-signer authorization without protocol changes.  - Community feedback, technical input, and interoperable implementations are required for broad adoption and practical standardization.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Stale Tip Relay
active_posts.summary: - The `staletip` proposal aims to improve monitoring of stale rates and block propagation issues in Bitcoin.  - It enables nodes to exchange recent stale tip information using an optional peer-to-peer messaging system.  - Technical constraints include message size limits, active tip proximity, and a cache for recent stale tips.

active_posts.title: [bitcoindev]
active_posts.summary: - A draft aims to standardize enforcement policies for co-signers to enhance interoperability across blockchains.  - The draft proposes compatibility with diverse verification methods and requires script-enforceable conditions within scripts.  - Feedback is sought regarding policy serialization, verification formats, output languages, and timelock fallback necessity.

active_posts.title: Quantum Landmines and Vulnerable Coin Auctions
active_posts.summary: - Post-quantum proposals use incentives and game theory to protect legacy cryptocurrency outputs from quantum attacks.  - Mechanisms include quantum landmines, staked auctions, and sats auctions with adaptive security features.  - No single solution fits all; priorities differ and strategies must evolve as threats change over time.

active_posts.title: Great Consensus Cleanup Revival
active_posts.summary: - The proposal identifies vulnerabilities in Bitcoin’s protocol and suggests improvements for network security and efficiency.  - Recommended changes include fixing timewarp, constraining legacy scripts, and invalidating certain small transactions.  - Some suggestions, like reducing block size, have sparked debate due to concerns about scalability and functionality.

active_posts.title: Stats on compact block reconstructions
active_posts.summary: - The study analyzes block reconstruction efficiency, focusing on transaction sources and the need for additional requests.  - Node configuration changes, such as increased connections or enabling full-RBF, notably impacted reconstruction performance.  - Heightened mempool activity and network congestion led to reduced reconstruction success and greater performance disparities.

active_posts.title: Public key recovery for EC leaves in P2MR (BIP-360)
active_posts.summary: - The proposal introduces a recoverable elliptic curve leaf, enabling public key recovery from signatures.  - Witness size decreases by deducing public keys, maintaining security and simplifying validation logic within P2MR.  - A revised nonce derivation increases signing security, optimizing blockchain space and lowering transaction costs.

today_in_history_posts.title: BIP30 and BIP34 interaction (was Re: [BIP Proposal] Buried Deployments)
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Duplicate transaction hashes are permitted, and BIP34 does not prevent their occurrence.  - Coinbase transaction collisions are prevented through the inclusion of the committed height.  - Regular transaction collisions are unlikely because of input choices and entropy usage.

today_in_history_posts.title: LN without SegWit: less efficient or less secure?
today_in_history_posts.summary: - The email asks about SegWit activation and its relation to the Lightning Network's feasibility.  - It highlights concerns about the security and efficiency differences between Lightning Network level 2 and level 3.  - Clarification is requested about whether server-based channel monitoring addresses level 2 security concerns.

today_in_history_posts.title: Gossip Observer: New project to monitor the Lightning P2P network
today_in_history_posts.summary: - The project monitors Lightning gossip network message propagation, revealing reduced convergence delay and some connectivity inefficiencies.  - Channel_update and node_announcement messages show high repetition, raising concerns about rate limits and implementations.  - Future work includes expanding infrastructure, enabling broader data collection, and encouraging community engagement and analysis.
